title: Sahara Grand Crossing
excerpt: Fourteen days by camel, 4WD, and foot through Morocco's great desert — dunes, canyon, oasis, and stars that own the night.

itinerary.title: Marrakech Arrival
itinerary.description: Medina walk, evening brief in the riad. Mint tea, lantern light, the call to prayer from every direction.

itinerary.title: Atlas Mountains Crossing
itinerary.description: Over the Tizi n'Tichka pass. Berber villages clinging to cliffsides. The desert begins on the south side.

itinerary.title: Draa Valley
itinerary.description: 300km of palm oasis following the river south. Fortified kasbahs every few kilometers.

itinerary.title: Zagora — Edge of the Erg
itinerary.description: The last town before the dunes. Camel market in the morning. Departure into the desert after lunch.

itinerary.title: Into the Erg Chegaga
itinerary.description: Five hours by camel. Silence falls once the last road disappears behind the first dune crest.

itinerary.title: Deep Desert Camp
itinerary.description: No tracks, no structures, no horizon features — just dune geometry in every direction. Starfield begins at dusk.

itinerary.title: Sunrise Dune Summit
itinerary.description: 4am departure on foot. The dune summit at first light — cold wind, orange sky, shadow geometry.

itinerary.title: Hammada — Stone Desert
itinerary.description: The other Sahara. Flat black gravel plain, wind-carved rocks, fossilized sea creatures in the limestone.

itinerary.title: Oasis Rest Day
itinerary.description: Hidden freshwater spring. Date palms. Traditional Gnawa music in the evening. Full rest.

itinerary.title: Todra Gorge
itinerary.description: 300m vertical walls pressing in from both sides. Rock climbers on the walls. Trout in the stream.

itinerary.title: Dades Valley
itinerary.description: The Road of a Thousand Kasbahs. Dramatic switchbacks above the valley floor.

itinerary.title: Erg Chebbi — Merzouga
itinerary.description: The most famous dunes. Sunset colors that no photograph has ever fully captured.

itinerary.title: Northern Return — Fes
itinerary.description: Cross-country to Fes. The world's oldest university. Tanneries seen from the leather merchants' terraces.

itinerary.title: Marrakech Return
itinerary.description: Final debrief. Souk farewell. Return flights or onward travel.

included: All accommodation (riads in cities, desert camps under stars)
gear: Lightweight sun protection (long sleeves, hat with neck flap)
Dust goggles or sunglasses (sand can be intense)
Merino layers — desert nights are cold
Sturdy sandals or light hiking shoes
